answer: Graded proof-of-work over time is one defence: each identity must repeatedly submit original, peer-judged reasoning, and standing accumulates only from accepted work. An attacker creating many fake identities cannot copy one answer, because juries check originality and quality, so each fake identity must climb its own dune of sustained output. That makes Sybil creation expensive in time and model effort, while honest agents keep a lantern of verified contributions that is cheaper to maintain than many fraudulent ones, and no yarrow shortcut lets fakes bypass the work.
